# Copilot Instructions

- **Project shape**: Library for benchmarking Sudoku (and generic exact cover) on NISQ hardware. Public entrypoints are in [src/sudoku_nisq/__init__.py](src/sudoku_nisq/__init__.py): `QSudoku`, `QExactCover`, `ExactCoverQuantumSolver`, `ExactCoverProblem`, and optional `BackendManager`.
- **Core flow (Sudoku)**: [QSudoku](src/sudoku_nisq/q_sudoku.py) wraps a `SudokuPuzzle`, manages one active solver, and attaches backends. Call `set_solver(ExactCoverQuantumSolver, encoding="simple"|"pattern", **opts)` then `build_circuit(...)/run(...)`. Puzzle hashes drive caching.
- **Core flow (generic exact cover)**: [QExactCover](src/sudoku_nisq/q_exact_cover.py) wraps an `ExactCoverProblem`, preconfigures `ExactCoverQuantumSolver(encoding="simple")`, and exposes `build_circuit(sdk=...)`, `run_aer`, and `report_resources` for non-Sudoku instances.
- **Encoding**: [ExactCoverEncoding](src/sudoku_nisq/encodings/exact_cover_encoding.py) builds `simple_subsets` and `pattern_subsets`; 2×2 puzzles use reduced constraints (`universe2x2`). Pattern encoding is based on row-pattern reduction (Weiß 2022).
- **Solver**: [ExactCoverQuantumSolver](src/sudoku_nisq/solvers/exact_cover_solver.py) extends [QuantumSolver](src/sudoku_nisq/quantum_solver.py), supports Sudoku mode or generic exact-cover mode. Options: `decompose_cnz` (default True for consistent gate counts) and `track_memory` (optional psutil-based snapshots). Gate counts and memory stats are stored on the instance.
- **Circuit builds**: `QuantumSolver.build_main_circuit(backend=None, sdk=None, force_overwrite=False)` auto-detects SDK (default PyTKET). Explicit `sdk="qiskit"|"pytket"|"braket"` always rebuilds and returns native circuit types; cache is stored as flattened PyTKET JSON under `.quantum_solver_cache/{puzzle_hash}/{solver}/{encoding}`.
- **Transpilation**: `_transpile_qiskit` uses `generate_preset_pass_manager` when the backend exposes a `Target`; otherwise falls back to `qiskit.compiler.transpile`. `_transpile_pytket` delegates to backend `get_compiled_circuit`. Braket pre-transpilation is unsupported by design.
- **Backends**: Use the singleton `BackendManager.inst()` ([backends.py](src/sudoku_nisq/backends.py)) which registers provider implementations from [src/sudoku_nisq/providers](src/sudoku_nisq/providers). Aer is always present; IBM/Quantinuum/AWS are optional (import may be None). `init_aer` accepts `method/noise_model/coupling_map/basis_gates/device_type/precision`. `get_backend_sdk(alias)` returns provider SDK without heuristic detection.
- **Providers**: Providers share the `QuantumProvider` interface ([providers/base.py](src/sudoku_nisq/providers/base.py)). IBM path uses native `qiskit_ibm_runtime`; Quantinuum path depends on PyTKET extensions; AWS path uses Braket SDK. Expect `NotImplementedError` or missing imports if optional deps are absent—guard with try/except or feature flags.
- **Puzzle generation**: [SudokuPuzzle](src/sudoku_nisq/sudoku_puzzle.py) supports `size` (2 or perfect squares) or `subgrid_size`; `canonicalize=True` relabels digits. `open_tuples` enumerates valid placements; `pre_tuples` lists givens; `get_hash()` seeds cache paths.
- **Metadata & caching**: [MetadataManager](src/sudoku_nisq/metadata_manager.py) lazily loads/saves JSON with atomic writes. Paths live under `.quantum_solver_cache/{puzzle_hash}/metadata.json`; solver/circuit resources are nested by solver and encoding. Use `ensure_puzzle_fields` before storing solver resources to keep metadata coherent.
- **Gate-building backends**: Circuit constructors live in [src/sudoku_nisq/circuits/exact_cover](src/sudoku_nisq/circuits/exact_cover); PyTKET and Qiskit implementations return `(circuit, gate_counts)`. Braket currently reuses PyTKET build.
- **Examples**: End-to-end workflows live in [examples/](examples/) (e.g., `exact_cover_benchmark.py`, `canonical_encoding_demo.py`) and mirror README snippets.
- **Docs**: Public docs build with `poetry run sphinx-build docs docs/_build`. Internal metrics design lives in [docs/internal/architecture](docs/internal/architecture) and is excluded from published docs.
- **Tests**: Run `poetry run pytest`. Some suites are skipped while `BackendManager` refactors (see [tests/test_backends.py](tests/test_backends.py)); IBM/Quantinuum paths are heavily mocked, so network creds are not required for defaults.
- **Dependencies**: Python 3.11–3.12; Poetry manages deps. Heavy extras (pytket, qiskit-aer, mitiq, amazon-braket-sdk) are in the main dependency list; ensure the environment can compile/install them before running full test/doc builds.
- **Common pitfalls**: (1) Cache collisions—explicit `sdk` forces rebuild, so beware stale PyTKET cache when switching SDKs; (2) Provider imports may be `None` when packages missing—wrap optional flows; (3) 2×2 puzzles skip subgrid constraints; (4) Braket has no client-side transpilation—don’t expect transpiled cache.
- **Style**: Keep cache and metadata paths stable; prefer existing public APIs instead of reaching into solver internals. Add concise docstrings; follow existing type hints and PyTKET/Qiskit naming.
